prompt: Build a repeating-key XOR cipher over character codes: each character is combined with the next key character, and applying the same key twice returns the original text.
explanation: XOR flips exactly the bits that are 1 in the key, and flipping the same bits a second time restores the original, which is why encryption and decryption are the same method here. Cycling the key with i % key.length() lets a short key cover a long message, and it is also why an empty key has to be rejected -- the remainder by zero would throw. Masking with & 0xFF keeps every result inside one byte so the values round-trip cleanly through char.
hints: Guard the empty key first, otherwise i % key.length() divides by zero.
Inside the loop: text.charAt(i) ^ key.charAt(i % key.length()), then & 0xFF.
toText appends (char) code for each value; a StringBuilder makes that cheap.
